scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

First, the family has a long-standing tradition of hosting Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve, which was taken over by the siblings after their mom got too old. The rotation system was agreed upon, and each sibling has hosted one holiday so far. This implies that there was a mutual understanding and agreement to take turns. The person's decision to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade with their wife's family seems to be a significant event for them, especially since it's a "once in a lifetime event" for their daughter. It's understandable that they would want to prioritize this experience, especially since it's something their daughter might not get another chance to do. However, by deciding to go, the person is essentially backing out of their turn to host Thanksgiving. This could disrupt the rotation system that was in place, potentially causing inconvenience and frustration for the other siblings, particularly the oldest sister who is now being asked to host again, even though it's not her turn. The person did try to offer solutions, like paying for a catered event, but the sister felt that this would take away from the close-knit family vibe. The person also offered to host the next holiday, but the sister refused, stating that it's her turn and she's been planning for it all year. The brother suggested swapping Thanksgivings, but it's unclear if the wife is up for it, and the brother didn't sound too happy about it. So, is the person in the wrong? On the other hand, they're disrupting a family tradition and potentially causing stress and inconvenience for their siblings, especially the oldest sister who is already planning for her turn. It's also worth considering the mother's feelings, as the sister mentioned that the mother wouldn't abandon Thanksgiving to go to NYC. This adds another layer of guilt and responsibility for the person. In terms of fairness, the rotation system was in place to distribute the responsibility equally among the siblings. By backing out, the person is shifting the burden onto another sibling, which could lead to resentment. However, the person did try to mitigate the situation by offering solutions and being willing to host the next holiday, which shows that they're not completely disregarding their responsibilities. The fact that the sister refused to swap or accept the offer to host next time complicates things further.
